title: Trading Policy
date_next_review: Reviewed by the Board once every three years, or more frequently if required

tiers.name: Prescribed Persons
tiers.description: Directors, Senior Management, employees reporting directly to Senior Management, anyone notified in writing by the Company Secretary or Senior Management that they are subject to pre-clearance, and any Helia Employee in possession of Inside Information. Subject to pre-clearance under section 4.1 and hedging/margin lending consent under section 4.4.

tiers.name: Helia Employees
tiers.description: All employees, officers and directors of Helia and its subsidiaries, and consultants, independent contractors and advisers working directly for Helia under a contract other than employment, together with each of their Associates. Subject to Trading Windows, no short-term/speculative dealing or short selling, and the hedging/margin lending consent requirement.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company or its subsidiaries; a Prescribed Person, and also subject to the Minimum Shareholding Policy and specified in the pre-clearance approver table.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A spouse, de facto partner, domestic partner, civil union partner, or dependent under 18, of any Helia Employee, any other relative living in the same household (unless financially independent), or any other person whose investment decisions a Helia Employee may influence.

definitions.hedging_definition: any arrangement (with anyone) that has the effect of limiting the exposure of the Helia Employee to risk relating to Helia Securities

windows.start_anchor: beginning of trade on the second trading day following the announcement on ASX of Helia's half year or full year results
windows.end_anchor: 4 weeks after the Trading Window opens

windows.start_anchor: second trading day following Helia's Annual General Meeting
windows.end_anchor: 2 weeks after the Trading Window opens

windows.start_anchor: commencement of an offer period for Securities under a prospectus, PDS, cleansing notice or other disclosure document

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board must resolve for a Trading Window to open at all, and may direct the Company Secretary to inform relevant individuals if it does not open a particular Window; that fact is confidential. The Company Secretary may also declare at any time that an open Trading Window has closed, and this fact, and the existence of a resulting Dealing restriction, may itself be Inside Information and must be kept confidential.

rules.detail: 'Other transactions' expressly includes derivatives-based transactions or arrangements including options and warrant contracts relating to Helia; Securities is defined to include contracts for difference and other derivatives. No venue limitation, so an OTC put/call is caught. Prescribed Persons need pre-clearance and must Deal only in a Trading Window; other Helia Employees need only observe Trading Windows unless they are Prescribed Persons.
rules.evidence: any derivatives-based or other transaction or arrangement, including in relation to debentures, options to subscribe for new shares and options over existing shares and warrant contracts relating to Helia.

rules.detail: Express, broadly-drafted prohibition on entering or agreeing to enter any hedging arrangement in relation to Helia Securities without the prior written consent of the Table 1 Approver, applying to all Helia Employees (not just Prescribed Persons) and not distinguishing unvested from vested holdings.
rules.evidence: Helia Employees must not, without the prior written consent of the Approvers set out in Table 1 above, enter into or agree to enter into: (a) any hedging arrangements in relation to any Helia Securities (including any arrangement (with anyone) that has the effect of limiting the exposure of the Helia Employee to risk relating to Helia Securities)

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A forward sale or similar arrangement over Helia Securities would be an 'other transaction' (derivatives-based transaction or arrangement) and, because it operates to limit the employee's risk exposure, would also be a hedging arrangement requiring the Table 1 Approver's prior written consent.
rules.evidence: any arrangement (with anyone) that has the effect of limiting the exposure of the Helia Employee to risk relating to Helia Securities

rules.detail: Outright ban on short selling any Helia Securities, alongside the ban on short-term/speculative dealing; no clearance route is offered for short selling itself.
rules.evidence: Helia Employees must not Deal in Helia Securities on a short-term basis or for speculative trading gain and must not engage in ‘short selling’ any Helia Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named and is not obviously caught by the Dealing definition (applying for, acquiring or disposing of Securities) or by 'other transactions'.

Contracts for difference are expressly named within the definitions of Securities and Helia Securities, so a CFD is an 'other transaction' under 2.2; Prescribed Persons require pre-clearance and it may also be caught by the hedging consent requirement if it limits risk exposure.
rules.evidence: Helia Securities includes Helia shares, debentures, options to subscribe for new shares and options over existing shares, warrant contracts, contracts for difference and other derivatives relating to Helia shares.

rules.detail: Margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in connection with Helia Securities require prior written consent of the Table 1 Approver; not an outright ban. Applies to all Helia Employees, not only Prescribed Persons, and is not stated to distinguish vesting state.
rules.evidence: any margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in connection with any Helia Securities.

rules.detail: Encumbrance is not named separately from 'secured financing arrangements'; granting security over Helia Securities to a lender falls within that phrase and so requires prior written consent.
rules.evidence: any margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in connection with any Helia Securities.

rules.detail: Broad express category ('other secured financing arrangements in connection with any Helia Securities') requiring the Table 1 Approver's prior written consent; the applicant must provide full details and reasons why consent is appropriate. No blanket prohibition and no exemption authority stated for this category specifically.
rules.evidence: Any request of the Company Secretary for consent to the above arrangements should include full details of the proposed arrangements and provide reasons why giving consent is appropriate.

rules.detail: Ban on Dealing on a short-term basis or for speculative gain; guidance describes short-term trading as Dealing intended or perceived to realise a gain from particular information or circumstances rather than long-term fundamentals. No fixed holding period stated and no carve-out identified for plan securities.
rules.evidence: Generally, short term trading is Dealing that has the intention or the effect (or may be perceived to have the intention or the effect) of realising a gain due to particular information or circumstances and not an investment based on long term fundamentals.

clearance.evidence: Chair and their Associates – Approver: Chair of the Audit Committee.

clearance.tier: Chief Executive Officer and their Associates
clearance.evidence: Chief Executive Officer and their Associates – Approver: Chair of the Board.

clearance.tier: Directors (excluding the Chair) and their Associates
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (per ASX Listing Rule 3.19B agreement)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as possible after the change occurs
clearance.evidence: The Directors of Helia must notify the Company Secretary if their interest in Helia’s Securities changes, as soon as possible after such change occurs and otherwise in accordance with their agreement with Helia under ASX Listing Rule 3.19B.
General Counsel and their Associates – Approver: Chair of the Board.
Company Secretary and their Associates – Approver: Chair of the Board.
All other Prescribed Persons – Approver: Company Secretary.

short_term.evidence: Generally, short term trading is Dealing that has the intention or the effect (or may be perceived to have the intention or the effect) of realising a gain due to particular information or circumstances and not an investment based on long term fundamentals.

exceptions.evidence: a disposal of Helia Securities arising from the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back or capital reduction
an acquisition of Helia Securities under a pro-rata issue, or a disposal of rights acquired under a pro-rata offer

an acquisition of any Helia Securities under a Helia employee incentive plan, including the acquisition of Helia Securities upon exercise of options or in satisfaction of rights to acquire shares, but excluding any trading in those Helia Securities after their acquisition

an acquisition of Helia Securities under any dividend reinvestment plan or security purchase plan (provided that the Helia Employee or their Associate did not commence or amend their participation in the dividend reinvestment plan outside of a Trading Window)
public offerings of Helia Securities to Helia Employees

indirect and incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of a Helia Employee trading securities issued by a management investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party and that happens to hold as part of its portfolio Helia Securities.
severe financial hardship where the sale of Helia Securities is the only practical method to meet a pressing or urgent financial commitment
a requirement to Deal in Helia Securities pursuant to a court order or a court enforceable undertaking
an overriding legal or regulatory requirement to transfer, or accept a transfer of, Helia Securities

financing.minimum_shareholding_requirement: Directors and certain Senior Management must comply with Helia's Minimum Shareholding Policy; a Pre-Trade Request that would cause them (or their Associates) to breach their minimum shareholding requirement will be rejected. Whether hedged shares are excluded from counting towards the requirement is not addressed.

exemption_authority: The Table 1 Approver (Chair of the Audit Committee, Chair of the Board, or Company Secretary depending on the applicant) may grant hedging/margin lending consent, pre-clearance, and exceptional-circumstances exemptions to trade outside a Trading Window, each in its absolute discretion and without giving reasons, and each revocable if new information or circumstances arise.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging and secured financing consent regime
bespoke_clauses.clause: Helia Employees must not, without the prior written consent of the Approvers set out in Table 1 above, enter into or agree to enter into: (a) any hedging arrangements in relation to any Helia Securities ...; or (b) any margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in connection with any Helia Securities. Any request ... should include full details of the proposed arrangements and provide reasons why giving consent is appropriate.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both legs of a funded collar (the hedge and the secured loan) are permitted only with prior written consent from a senior approver, on a full-disclosure, discretionary, no-reasons-required basis, so the bank's product would need to be presented in detail and could be refused or later revoked.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any trading pre-clearance, consent or exemption under this Policy can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Consent for the collar/loan structure is not durable; Helia can withdraw it mid-transaction or during the facility's life if circumstances change, creating unwind risk for the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and certain Senior Management must also comply with Helia’s Minimum Shareholding Policy and are not permitted to Deal in Helia Securities if such Dealing will cause them to breach their minimum shareholding requirement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar or its physical settlement/forced-sale counts as a Dealing that reduces the holding, it could breach the MSR and be blocked at pre-clearance stage regardless of hedging consent; the policy does not say whether hedged (but not disposed) shares still count.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no consent overrides insider trading law
bespoke_clauses.clause: Irrespective of the trading pre-clearance, consent, or an exemption under this Policy being granted, nothing in such pre-clearance, consent or exemption, or in this Policy, shall relieve or purport to relieve an individual from their obligations to comply with applicable Insider Trading laws or with the other sections of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even fully consented and pre-cleared, the collar's entry, unwind or roll must independently satisfy insider trading law each time, e.g. if inside information later arises.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company Secretary may declare at any time that a Trading Window has closed ... The fact that the Trading Window has closed and that there is a restriction on Dealing may itself constitute Inside Information ... and must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Trading Window can close without notice or public disclosure, so a collar counterparty relying on execution during an open window bears undisclosed timing risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: indirect and incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of a Helia Employee trading securities issued by a management investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party and that happens to hold as part of its portfolio Helia Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Confirms the exemption is narrow (incidental fund lookthrough only) and does not extend to a bespoke OTC collar structured through an intermediary vehicle.

summary: A funded collar is not prohibited outright under Helia's Trading Policy, but both legs require prior written consent. Section 4.4 requires Helia Employees to obtain the prior written consent of the relevant Table 1 Approver (Chair of the Audit Committee, Chair of the Board, or the Company Secretary, depending on seniority) before entering into any hedging arrangement or any margin lending or other secured financing arrangement in connection with Helia Securities, with full details and reasons to be provided; approval is discretionary, need not state reasons, and can be withdrawn if circumstances change. Because the arrangement is also a Dealing and, for Prescribed Persons, likely involves derivatives, it separately needs pre-clearance under section 4.1 and must be executed within a Trading Window (or under an exceptional-circumstances exemption) and outside possession of Inside Information. Directors and certain Senior Management must also not breach their Minimum Shareholding Policy requirement, which is not stated to exclude hedged shares. Overall, a funded collar is achievable in principle but is subject to full disclosure, senior-level sign-off, timing within a Trading Window, and revocability, with no guaranteed approval.
